findings.stemStart: An estate of barely more than three hectares
findings.problem: The exp called a whole appellation in one owner's hands 'very nearly unique in the country'. That overstates it: La Romanee-Conti, La Tache, La Grande Rue and Clos de Tart are monopole appellations in Burgundy, and so is Coulee de Serrant, one of the distractors.
findings.fix: Now: 'rare in France: La Romanee-Conti in Burgundy and Coulee de Serrant on the Loire are two of the very few others.' This also explains why that distractor looks plausible.
findings.source: Monopole AOCs: La Romanee-Conti (Burgundy grand cru) and Coulee de Serrant (AOC since 2011, held by one family)

findings.source: Hermitage lieux-dits: Rocoules is planted mostly, not only, to white varieties

findings.stemStart: Traditional northern cellars matured Syrah in large old
findings.problem: The stem says the cellars used large old casks 'rather than in new barriques', so 'A barrique' was ruled out by the stem's own words. 'A pupitre' is a riddling rack, not a vessel. That left foudre against amphora, which a student could get by elimination. The exp also used the US 'toward'.
findings.fix: Distractors now 'A feuillette' (a small cask of about 130 litres) and 'A concrete egg', so all four are wine vessels and only one is a large wooden cask. Key and its length unchanged. In the exp, 'toward' is now 'towards'.
findings.source: Cooperage terms: foudre (large cask or vat), feuillette (small cask of roughly 114 to 136 litres)

findings.stemStart: Plantings of one northern white had fallen to
findings.problem: The stem asks which northern white nearly died out, but one distractor (Counoise) is a black grape. That makes the options of mixed kind, and a student can drop it without knowing anything.
findings.fix: Counoise replaced by Clairette, a southern white that was never close to extinction. Key and exp unchanged.
findings.source: Ampelography: Counoise is black; Clairette is white and widely planted in the south

findings.stemStart: The minimum alcohol demanded there is the highest
findings.problem: The stem stated that Chateauneuf's 12.5 percent minimum is 'the highest of any French appellation'. That is false today: Sauternes and Barsac require 13 percent natural potential alcohol, and the vins doux naturels require far more. The exp also used the banned word ('In practice').
findings.fix: Stem now: 'A red from the papal village that falls short of a set natural alcohol may not carry the name. What is that minimum?' Key 12.5 percent and options unchanged. The exp opens 'Most wines land far above it'. Id moves i-5u8wquhp to i-dd77fiqp; check-similarity clean.
findings.source: Chateauneuf-du-Pape cahier des charges (12.5 percent natural minimum for red); Sauternes cahier des charges (13 percent natural minimum)

findings.problem: The exp grouped Bourboulenc with the grapes that 'give weight rather than tension'. Bourboulenc is the one grown in the south mainly for its freshness and acidity.
findings.fix: Now: 'Grenache Blanc, Clairette and Roussanne give weight rather than tension, with Bourboulenc lending some freshness.'
findings.source: Variety profile: Bourboulenc keeps its acidity late and is valued for freshness (Chateauneuf, La Clape)

findings.problem: The exp said dorado was aged 'under a film of yeast'. That contradicts its own key ('An oxidatively aged white called dorado'). Rueda Dorado is the oxidative style; the flor-aged style is Rueda Palido.
findings.fix: Now: 'Dorado was aged oxidatively, first in glass demijohns left out in the sun and then in cask, which brings it closer to a Sherry than to any modern white. A little is still made, beside a flor-aged cousin called Palido.'
findings.source: Rueda DO pliego de condiciones: Dorado (oxidative ageing) and Palido (biological ageing under flor)

findings.stemStart: A butt marked for Fino loses its flor
findings.problem: The stem said a Palo Cortado loses its flor 'without ever being refortified'. That is wrong: once the flor fails and the cellar master reclassifies the butt, it is fortified to about 17 percent or more to age oxidatively. The exp implied the same thing.
findings.fix: Stem now: 'A butt set aside for Fino loses its flor early and unbidden, then finishes with the nose of an Amontillado over the body of an Oloroso. Which style is it?' The exp now says a Palo Cortado 'loses its flor by accident and is fortified only afterwards, to age with oxygen'. Options and key unchanged. Id moves i-lfjnphqw to i-jdo79slb; check-similarity clean.
findings.source: Consejo Regulador Jerez-Xeres-Sherry account of Palo Cortado: reclassified from the biological line and fortified for oxidative ageing

verdicts.stemStart: Almost every cru of the northern valley sits
verdicts.why: The direction of the river's bend at Tain is told both ways in print, so dropping it was wise. The replacement is plain geography: the vineyard runs from Les Bessards in the west to the eastern lieux-dits, so the face looks south over Tain, and it agrees with the module's own 'western end' Bessards question.

verdicts.stemStart: An estate of barely more than three hectares
verdicts.why: The fix is right: monopole appellations are few but more than one (La Romanee-Conti, La Tache, La Grande Rue, Clos de Tart, La Romanee, Coulee de Serrant), and a search confirms Coulee de Serrant is still one family's whole appellation, so naming it explains the distractor while the stem's 'within the boundaries of Condrieu' still decides it. Amended only for voice: 'rare in France' followed 'smallest appellations in France' in the sentence before, so it now reads 'rare in the country'.

verdicts.why: Banned word in the stem, no other route; 'is common in the north' says the same and whole-bunch inclusion is indeed traditional there. Id loss logged and accepted.

verdicts.stemStart: Traditional northern cellars matured Syrah in large old
verdicts.why: The original was answerable by elimination: the stem itself ruled out the barrique and a pupitre is a riddling rack. A feuillette is a real small cask, so a student must know foudre means large; concrete egg and amphora are real vessels. The build reports no length signal and 'towards' is the British form.

verdicts.stemStart: Plantings of one northern white had fallen to
verdicts.why: Removing Counoise was right (a black grape among whites answers itself). But Clairette made this question's four options identical to the co-ferment question's, with the same Viognier key, and to the Marsanne question's as well, so a student could answer by recognising the set. Grenache Blanc, a widely planted southern white never near extinction, does the same work without the repeat; key and exp unchanged.

verdicts.stemStart: The minimum alcohol demanded there is the highest
verdicts.why: The superlative was false (Sauternes asks 13 percent natural, the vins doux naturels far more) and sat in the stem, so the stem had to change; 'there' also had no referent in a shuffled pool and 'the papal village' does. Twelve and a half percent natural remains the Chateauneuf minimum, and 'a natural alcohol' is ordinary trade usage. The banned word left the exp too.

verdicts.stemStart: Before Verdejo was replanted, Rueda's reputation rested on
verdicts.why: The original contradicted its own key. A search confirms the Rueda rules keep Dorado as oxidative ageing (at least four years, the last two in oak) and Palido as biological ageing under flor, both still made; the demijohns in the sun are the traditional first stage.

verdicts.stemStart: A butt marked for Fino loses its flor
verdicts.why: 'Without ever being refortified' was wrong: once the flor fails and the butt is reclassified it is fortified to about 17 percent or more for oxidative ageing. The error was in the stem, so the stem had to change; the new stem and exp state the accident and the later fortification correctly. 'Marked' to 'set aside' was incidental to a needed rewrite.
